root_cause.text: In `drivers/md/md-llbitmap.c`’s `llbitmap_read_page()`, the member-disk selection logic failed to reject `rdev`s that were not `In_sync`, so it could read bitmap pages from spare/rebuilding disks that do not yet contain valid bitmap data.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `!test_bit(In_sync, &rdev->flags)` to the existing filter (`rdev->raid_disk < 0 || test_bit(Faulty, &rdev->flags)`), and the commit message states the bug was that the code “only checks for raid_disk assignment and Faulty flag, missing the In_sync flag check,” allowing reads from “spare disks that are still being rebuilt and don't have valid bitmap information yet.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Skip non-in-sync RAID devices when reading bitmap pages to avoid using unsynchronized members.
intent_record.what: The condition inside the `rdev_for_each(rdev, mddev)` loop in `llbitmap_read_page()` was extended. It previously skipped devices when `rdev->raid_disk < 0` or `Faulty` was set; it now also skips devices when `In_sync` is not set.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the bitmap page read logic will ignore any array member that is not currently marked in-sync, preventing it from using devices that are present but not yet synchronized. This narrows the set of devices considered valid sources for bitmap-related reads.

grouping_result.intent: Skip non-in-sync RAID devices when reading bitmap pages to avoid using unsynchronized members.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: it fixes llbitmap_read_page() member-disk selection by skipping rdevs that are not In_sync, preventing reads from spare/rebuilding disks with invalid bitmap data.

candidates.rationale: This pre-fix selection filter rejected only invalid or faulty devices, but not devices that were still not In_sync. As a result, llbitmap_read_page() could choose a spare or rebuilding member and read bitmap pages from disk state that was not yet valid.

vuln_statements.explanation: This condition was the member-disk filter in llbitmap_read_page(), but it only excluded invalid or Faulty devices. It did not reject rdevs that were not In_sync, allowing spare or rebuilding disks to be selected and their bitmap pages read even though that data was not yet valid.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct is present in `llbitmap_read_page()`. The function iterates all member devices with `rdev_for_each(rdev, mddev)` and only filters `rdev->raid_disk < 0` and `test_bit(Faulty, &rdev->flags)`: `if (rdev->raid_disk < 0 || test_bit(Faulty, &rdev->flags)) continue;`. There is no check that the device is `In_sync` before issuing `sync_page_io(rdev, sector, PAGE_SIZE, page, REQ_OP_READ, true)`, so spare/rebuilding disks can be selected as the source of bitmap pages. The shown code does not contain any fix for this; the missing `In_sync` rejection is not present, and there is no additional guard in this function preventing reads from non-in-sync rdevs.
